content.thinking:
I'm looking at the incident: the monthly-spend feature flag was switched on at 11:48 by an admin, and that's what started the ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py. The flag split shows roughly 111 off and 89 on at 11:48, then every evaluation returned on from 11:49. Argus reverted the flag at 11:55, after the P2 alert fired just before.

I'm checking whether the revert reached the service: at 11:56 the evaluations still read the flag as on, so the rollback likely didn't propagate. Errors are still showing up, so I'm treating the flag as the live cause and planning to switch it off again and confirm that the evaluation log reads off and the ZeroDivisionError stops.

I'm working through the causal chain now: the shoppers' account page requests failed, which traces back to the ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py at 11:48. I'm checking whether the monthly-spend flag change at 11:48 is what drove that path, and I'm ruling out an earlier deploy since none turned up in the window.

I'm tracing the root cause now: the flag-on path calls average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides by the number of purchases this month, so shoppers with no purchases this month trigger the ZeroDivisionError. I'm checking that the earlier deploy window turned up nothing, since the flag was off and the service healthy before 11:48.

I'm laying out the causal chain now. The account page requests failed with the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 starting at 11:48, and that path only ran once the service began evaluating the monthly-spend flag as on after the admin switched it on. Before that switch the flag read off and the pages rendered normally, and I'm noting that no earlier deploy turned up in the window.

I'm lining up the causal chain now: the ZeroDivisionError only happens on the flag-on path, which divides by this month's purchase count, so shoppers with no purchases this month hit it. I'm checking that the flag-on path is what the service ran after the admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at 11:48, and that no earlier deploy turned up in the window.

I'm tying the ZeroDivisionError to the flag: the flag-on path divides by this month's purchase count, which is zero for shoppers who haven't bought anything this month. The flag was read on from 11:48, and the admin's switch at that time is the change that brought that path into play.

I'm drafting the plain-language summary now: the switch-on of the monthly spending summary likely made the account page divide by this month's purchase count, which fails for shoppers who haven't bought anything yet this month. I'm also noting that the flag was put back on while the errors continued, so the account pages could keep failing until the fault is fixed.

I'm now listing the contributing factors: first, no check seems to have exercised the monthly-spend path for shoppers with no purchases this month before the flag went live, and second, the flag went to all traffic within a minute with no gradual rollout or automatic stop.

I'm weighing the remaining contributing factors: the alert didn't route to anyone on call, so nobody was paged to switch the flag off sooner, and I'm considering whether the revert failing to reach the service belongs with these or with the response.

I'm settling the action items now: one to add a pre-enable check that runs tests on flag-on paths, including accounts with no purchases this period, and another to roll out io-shop flags gradually with an automatic switch-off when the account page error rate rises.

I'm drafting the lessons section now, starting with what went well: the investigator placed the onset at the minute the flag was switched on, and Argus reverted the flag.

I'm drafting the lessons: the investigator placed the onset at the minute the flag was switched on, and Argus's revert was a good mitigation step. Next I'm listing what went wrong: the mitigation agent judged the revert refuted even though the service's own log still showed the flag as on at 11:56, so it never confirmed the change had reached the service before ruling on it.

I'm noting that the flag was put back on while the service was already evaluating it as on, so the mitigation step may have changed nothing. I'm also wondering whether the earlier incident's refuted revert of the same flag had the same propagation problem, and I think it deserves a line in the went-wrong section.

I'm noting the last thought was about whether to mention PR numbers in the write-up, since a number with a digit is a figure I'd rather leave out of the lessons section.

I'm checking which lessons the postmortem should record: the investigator placed the onset right at the flag switch, and the mitigation agent judged the revert refuted without confirming it reached the service, since the service's own log still read the flag as on at 11:56. I'm also thinking about the stop-the-harm step: switching the flag off again and confirming in the service's evaluation log that it now reads off.

I'm now checking the stop-the-harm step and the why-it-did-not-help item, and I'm working out which deploy evidence to cite for ruling out a code change, since two deploys appear in the evidence and I'll name the rows that show them.

I'm citing the two deploy rows that show no code change was found in the window, and noting that no earlier changes appear in the record.

action_items.item: Require passing tests of a feature flag's on path, including accounts with no purchases in the current period, before the flag can be switched on in production for io-shop.
Roll out io-shop feature flags to a small share of traffic first, and widen them only while the error rate stays at its usual level.
Switch a feature flag off automatically when the io-shop error rate rises during its rollout.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to the on-call rota, so that it pages a person.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The service's own warning on the account page error rate climbed from its usual level to its highest at {Gbac1.7}, and failed account page requests were logged from {G5309.3}.

The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError: division by zero in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, at line {F1.1}. This first appeared in the minute {G5309.3} and was still being logged at {G5309.6}.

That code ran because the service had started evaluating monthly-spend-feature as on. Before the onset, every evaluation read it as off and account pages rendered normally. In the minute {G971b.6} some evaluations read it as on, and from {Gce95.4} every evaluation did.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: the production change events read on both passes held only flag changes, and no deploy came back.

causal_chain.step: The service evaluated the flag as on because an admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}.

Turning the flag on broke the service because the spend-summary path it enables divides by the number of purchases a shopper made this month, which is zero for shoppers who have not bought anything this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Someone switched on a new monthly spending summary for shoppers' account pages, and the code behind it likely divides by the number of things a shopper bought this month, which breaks the page for shoppers who have not bought anything yet this month.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that exercised the code path monthly-spend-feature enables, such as a shopper with no purchases this month, before the flag was switched on in production.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been found before the flag reached shoppers, and the flag would not have been switched on with the fault in place.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went to all of the service's traffic almost at once. Some evaluations read it as on in its first minute, and every evaluation did from the next minute. No gradual rollout or automatic stop was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have reached the failing path, and the rollout could have been stopped once the error rate rose.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been brought in to switch the flag off and confirm the service took the change, instead of the service being left failing with the flag on.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident in the same minute the flag was switched on.
The Mitigation Agent reverted monthly-spend-feature, the change the evidence pointed to, and the revert can be undone.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix for the failing line as a draft pull request for a person to review.

went_wrong: The Mitigation Agent judged the flag revert refuted while the service's own log still showed every evaluation reading monthly-spend-feature as on at {Gce95.7}, after the revert. The revert was judged without anyone seeing the service take it. The flag was then put back on, and the second investigation came back with the same candidate.

input.root_cause: In src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, `average_spend_per_item_this_month`, which `render_spend_summary` reaches only when `use_monthly_summary` is true and `use_typical_spend` is false (the path monthly-spend-feature turns on), divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of purchases made this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is zero, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1}, and the error reaches the account page and fails the request.
input.still_at_risk: Account pages could keep failing for shoppers as long as monthly-spend-feature stays on, and the same failure could come back any time the flag is switched on before the fault is fixed.
input.stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. Confirm at the service that its flag-evaluation log reads monthly-spend-feature=off for every evaluation, that the ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py stops, and that the account page error rate falls back to its level before the onset.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
input.why_it_did_not_help: Find out whether the revert of monthly-spend-feature reached the service, since the service's log still showed the flag evaluated as on at {Gce95.7}, after the revert. If it did reach the service, find out why account page requests kept failing with ZeroDivisionError.
